title: 🛒 Typical Products
subtitle: The gastronomic excellence of Serracapriola and the Daunia Apennines

products.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil
products.desc: Serracapriola is a land of millenary olive trees. The local oil, with its fruity and light flavour, is produced by historic mills in the area. Ogliarola and Peranzana varieties, hand-picked every autumn.

products.name: Bread & Bakery
products.desc: Serracapriola's bread is wood-fired, made with local durum wheat flour. Fragrant outside, soft inside, it keeps for days. Also typical are friselle and rustic country bread.

products.name: Taralli
products.desc: Apulian taralli are the symbol of local street food: kneaded with olive oil, white wine and fennel, then boiled and baked until golden. Crunchy and irresistible. Where to find them: I Taralli di Zio Pino, Via Cavalier de Luca 20, tel. 347 665 2559 (please check the number first).

products.name: Pampanella
products.desc: Pampanella is a typical dish of the area: pork marinated with chilli pepper, garlic and vinegar, slowly cooked in the oven. Tasty and spicy, it is the star of village festivals.

products.name: Cruschi Peppers ("Diavlill")
products.desc: Cruschi peppers — called "diavlill" in local dialect — are sweet peppers dried in the sun and then fried in boiling oil until ultra-crispy and crumbly. A burst of sweet-smoky flavour, used as a starter, crumbled on pasta, eggs or simply as a snack. A Slow Food Presidium, they are one of the most authentic symbols of Daunia's peasant cuisine.

products.name: Sausage & Charcuterie
products.desc: The local sausage is made with selected pork, chilli pepper, fennel and local spices. Fresh or aged, it accompanies pasta and grills. Also artisanal capocollo and soppressata.

products.name: Wine
products.desc: The territory produces robust and fragrant wines based on Nero di Troia and Montepulciano d'Abruzzo grapes. Genuine reds, rosés and whites, ideal with local cuisine.

products.name: Pasta & Orecchiette
products.desc: Handmade orecchiette and cavatelli are still rolled by local housewives. Dressed with lamb ragù, turnip tops or fresh tomato from the Tavoliere plain, they are the heart of Serracapriola's cuisine.

products.name: Torcinelli
products.desc: Torcinelli are one of the oldest and most identity-defining dishes of the local cuisine. Lamb or kid offal — liver, lung, heart — wrapped in intestines and cooked on the grill or in a pan with garlic, parsley and chilli. Intense and rustic flavour, symbol of the peasant cooking of the Daunia Apennines.

products.name: Zeppole di San Giuseppe
products.desc: Zeppole di San Giuseppe are the classic Father's Day pastry (19 March). Choux pastry, fried or baked, filled with custard cream and sour cherries in syrup. In Serracapriola they are still made at home with grandmothers' recipes, soft inside and golden outside.

products.name: Mostaccioli
products.desc: Mostaccioli are hard, spiced biscuits typical of southern Italy, made with grape must, flour, almonds, cinnamon, cloves and pepper. In Serracapriola they are made for festivities and keep for a long time. Every family has its own recipe passed down through generations.

products.name: Almond Sweets
products.desc: Almond sweets are among the most refined specialities of local pastry-making. Almond pastes perfumed with orange blossom water, hand-moulded into fruit or flower shapes and decorated with coloured sugar. Soft outside, intensely aromatic inside — unmissable at weddings and festivals.

products.name: Pasticciotti
products.desc: A pasticciotto is a buttery shortcrust shell filled with thick custard cream, baked until golden. Typical of Puglia and Salento, it has also found its way onto Serracapriola's tables, becoming one of the most beloved pastries for young and old — perfect for breakfast or a snack.

products.name: Caciocavallo
products.desc: Podolico caciocavallo is the king of cheeses from the Daunia Apennines. Made with milk from free-ranging Podolica cows, it has an intense and slightly spicy flavour. Fresh or aged, also smoked.
